Revised assessment using FSR context: The April 29, 2020 FOMC statement accurately flags severe near- and medium-term downside risks from the pandemic and lays out an aggressive easing package (ELB policy rate, outcome-based forward guidance, large-scale Treasury and agency MBS/CMBS purchases, and ample repo/ON RRP operations) aimed at stabilizing markets and supporting credit transmission.

The concurrent Financial Stability Report underscores why the balance of risks was skewed to the downside despite these actions: it documents acute funding strains in short-term U.S. dollar markets, impaired Treasury market functioning, and heightened funding risk; elevated nonfinancial corporate leverage and rising solvency risk for households and businesses; and vulnerable asset valuations with wider external finance premia. These vulnerabilities can amplify shocks and weigh on the outlook, even as policy backstops help restore market functioning and compress term/credit spreads.

Netting these considerations, the tone remains negative overall—mitigated by strong policy support but tempered by elevated vulnerabilities noted in the FSR. Adjusting for the FSR’s added downside risks, the sentiment is slightly more negative than a policy-only read.
